contexts.text: As the man now begins to be made alive... he is compared first to the creeping things of the waters ().
The creeping things which the waters brought forth = scientifics, which are of the external man... That the creeping things of the waters, or fishes, = scientifics. Illustrated.

The things of the understanding are signified by the creeping things which the waters cause to creep forth, etc... Those of the will, are here signified by the living soul which the land produces, and by the beast, and creeping thing ().

From man to beast, and even to the creeping thing () = that whatever is of the will would extinguish him... Whatever is of the will is called beasts, and creeping things; here, creeping things = pleasures both corporeal and sensuous.

Bird = intellectual, and beast, voluntary things; and that the creeping thing of the ground () = both, but the lowest, may be evident from the fact, that the creeping thing of the ground is the lowest.

Everything that creeps upon the ground () = what is sensuous... The most ancients compared the sensuous things of man and his pleasurable ones to creeping things and creeping things, and so called them, because they are the outermost things, and as it were creep on the surface of a man, and because they are not permitted to raise themselves higher.

Every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth () = every sensuous and corporeal good... the creeping thing is mentioned last... Animals, beasts, and creeping things that creep on the land = voluntary things.

As to... every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth, etc. () = their persuasions; in which... the creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth = corporeal and earthly things... The persuasions of the Antediluvians are here fully described...
Creeping thing () = pleasures.

Bird = the intellectual, and beast the voluntary things of his internal man; and every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth () = like things corresponding to them in the external man; for in this passage, the creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth relates to both the bird, or intellectual things, and to the beast, or voluntary things. The most ancients called sensuous things and the pleasures of the body creeping things that creep, because they are just like creeping things that creep upon the earth... AC 911, Explained.

Every wild beast and every creeping thing () = his goods... The creeping thing = the goods of the external man. Every bird, and everything creeping upon the earth = truths... The thing creeping upon the earth = external truths... In the preceding verse, it was called the creeping thing that creepeth, because it signified both the good and the truth of the external man. Explained.
Everything that the ground maketh to creep forth () = the affections of good. Explained.

Every creeping thing that liveth () = all the pleasures in which there is good, which is alive. Creeping things, here, mean all clean beasts and birds, because it is said, they are given for meat. In the proper sense, creeping things are the lowest of all which are mentioned, ; and they were unclean things: but in a wider sense, as here, they are animals which are given for food; but are here called creeping things, because they = pleasures. Man's affections are signified by clean beasts, but as they are perceived only in his pleasures, and man therefore calls them pleasures, they are here called creeping things. Explained. AC 994:4.

Pleasures are also called creeping things in other parts of the Word; and a distinction is there made between clean and unclean creeping things; that is, between pleasures the delights of which are alive or heavenly, and those the delights of which are dead or infernal. Illustrated.
Every form of creeping thing () = filthy pleasures, the interiors of which are cupidities...
As creeping things = such filthy things, they were accounted so unclean in the representative Church, that no one was even allowed to touch them; and he who merely touched them was unclean. (.)
Creeping things = both the pleasures of the body, and the pleasures of sensuous things...
The dissent of the thoughts is perceived as something tacit that creeps.
The sensuous things of man were represented by serpents, because they are the lowest things with man... and as it were crawl...
The third degree is that frogs crept forth out of the waters. AC 9331:6.
The creeping thing of the land = the goods and truths of the external and sensuous man. References.
He would at first creep like a quadruped.
The popes then feel something turning and creeping in the abdomen.
The evil Genii... then appeared like creeping things in the streets, seeking with the greatest anxiety how to get out.
Everything that creepeth in the seas () = those who are sensuous.
A covenant with... the creeping thing of the land, etc. () = conjunction with... the affection of the Knowledges of truth and good of the Church.
Creeping thing, and bird of every wing () = the delight of good and truth of the natural and of the spiritual man.
The creeping thing that creepeth upon the land () = the Sensuous, which is the ultimate of the Natural, with the delights and scientifics there.
Creeping things () = living scientifics.
The creeping things of the land () = the things of the sensuous man: when separated from the spiritual man, these are merely falsities from evils.
Things creeping innumerable () = what is scientific there.
The creeping things () = the Sensuous, which is the ultimate of the natural man.
The creeping thing of the land () = the scientific of the natural man; in special, the scientific of the Sensuous. AE 701:20.
The creeping thing of the land () = the thoughts and affections in the corporeal Sensuous.
